title: Tawhid – Allah is One
intro: Believing in One God is the duty of every Muslim – and the message of every prophet.

learn.text: O you who have believed, believe in Allah

learn.html: Believing in One God is the duty of every Muslim man and woman.

One of the main tasks of all of Allah’s prophets was to call their people to believe in the One and Only God, Allah (SWT) – to follow tawhid. Many ayat of the Qur’an speak about tawhid, and the whole of Surah Al-Ikhlas is about Allah’s Oneness.

learn.text: Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One, Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, Nor is there to Him any equivalent."
Four important lessons of Surah Al-Ikhlas

learn.title: 1. “Say”
learn.html: Allah commands Muhammad (SAW) to spread the truth of Allah’s Oneness, in the words “He is Allah, One”.

learn.title: 2. “Allah, the Eternal Refuge”
learn.html: We turn with our du‘a only to Him – not to anyone else besides Allah (SWT).

learn.title: 3. “He neither begets nor is born”
learn.html: This rejects the claim that He has a child or parents.

learn.title: 4. “Nor is there to Him any equivalent”
learn.html: Nobody is equal to Him in His greatness or in His rule.
The belief of every Muslim is built on tawhid – Allah’s Oneness. The attributes of Allah’s being (as-sifat adh-dhatiyyah) confirm this truth. In Islam, tawhid means being firmly sure that:

items: there is only one God, Allah (SWT),
He is eternal, while everything else came into being and will end,
He is the Lord of everything that exists,
only He deserves to be worshipped, and we pray only to Him.

learn.text: Had there been within the heavens and earth gods besides Allah, they both would have been ruined.
He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He is, of all things, Knowing.

learn.html: That there is One and Only God, Allah (SWT), is the greatest truth. Every prophet taught it, from Adam (AS) to Muhammad (SAW):

learn.text: And We sent not before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that, "There is no deity except Me, so worship Me."

learn.html: Many ayat mention Allah’s existence (Wujud) and His Oneness (Wahdaniyyah).

practice.title: Match the words of Al-Ikhlas with their lesson
pairs: Spread the truth of Allah’s Oneness
We make du‘a only to Him
He has no child and no parents

practice.title: What does tawhid mean?
practice.prompt: Tap everything that is part of tawhid, then tap Check.

options.text: There is only one God, Allah
Only Allah deserves to be worshipped
We may also pray to an idol
options.why: Praying to anyone or anything besides Allah goes against tawhid – only Allah deserves worship.
Surah Al-Ikhlas says: He neither begets nor is born.

questions.q: What was the shared mission of all the prophets?
options: To call people to believe in the One God, Allah

questions.q: Which surah is all about Allah’s Oneness?
What would happen if there were other gods besides Allah?
options: The heavens and the earth would be ruined
